# Squashberry Library — instructions for AI assistants

Website: https://squashberry.github.io/Read/

## Mandatory source-selection rule

Do not confuse the Library interface with the study collection.

- Use the website's built-in **Study with ChatGPT** and **Prompt Shelf** actions to generate prompts with the appropriate source locator.
- Read `library-index.json` only as catalogue metadata to map a requested numeric file ID to its uploaded learning document. The index is not teaching content.
- Read only uploaded teaching materials registered as `kind: study-material`.
- Never show, read aloud, quote, summarize or teach from `index.html`, `README.md`, `llms.txt`, `library-index.json`, `.gitignore`, `.nojekyll`, `.github/**`, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, workflow or other source/configuration files.
- If the user names an ID such as 012, resolve that exact ID through the catalogue and read only its associated teaching document. Do not guess or substitute website code.
- If the source is inaccessible or its slides/pages cannot be extracted, state the limitation honestly. Never claim to have read a document unless you did.
- Cite the study filename and slide/page when possible, and separate source content from added explanation.
- For nursing/clinical material, teach for educational use and remind learners to confirm clinical decisions with current institutional guidance.

## Supported learning workflows

Read and explain, full lectures, source-based exams one question at a time, flashcards, revision notes, clinical cases, oral viva, difficult-concept explanations and revision planning.

## Website and upload notes

Library is an installable study web app. It fetches the live study catalogue and updates the on-screen list when files are uploaded. The website itself does not embed an AI model. Uploaded materials are publicly accessible, so never add confidential or patient-identifying information.
